target.title: fix(telegram): strip directive tags from prompt context dedupe key
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram assistant replies appear twice in prompt context — once from session transcript (with directive tags like `[[reply_to_current]]`) and once from the Telegram message cache (without tags). The dedupe key uses exact `timestamp_ms:body` matching, so `[[reply_to_current]]Hello` ≠ `Hello`.

Closes #99117

## Root Cause / Fix

`resolvePromptContextTextDedupeKey` compared raw message text including inline directive tags. Strip them with `stripInlineDirectiveTagsForDelivery` before computing the key so both copies produce the same key when visible text is identical.

**3 lines changed. No new module.**

## Evidence

### Production function proof

```bash
node --import tsx --no-warnings -e "
import { resolvePromptContextTextDedupeKey } from "./extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.runtime.js";

const sessionRow = { body: "[[reply_to_current]]Hello, world!", timestamp_ms: 1_778_474_760_000 };
const cacheRow = { body: "Hello, world!", timestamp_ms: 1_778_474_760_000 };

console.log("Session:", resolvePromptContextTextDedupeKey(sessionRow));
console.log("Cache:  ", resolvePromptContextTextDedupeKey(cacheRow));
console.log("Match:  ", resolvePromptContextTextDedupeKey(sessionRow) === resolvePromptContextTextDedupeKey(cacheRow) ? "✅" : "FAIL");
"
```

```
Session: 1778474760000:Hello, world!
Cache:   1778474760000:Hello, world!
Match:   ✅
```

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `[[reply_to_current]]Hello` vs `Hello` (same ts) | ❌ duplicate | ✅ deduped |
| `hello [[reply_to_current]] world` vs `hello world` | ❌ duplicate | ✅ deduped |
| `Hello` vs `Hello` (different ts) | ✅ separate | ✅ unchanged |

## Change Type
- [x] Bug fix
## Scope
- [x] Telegram channel (prompt context)
## Security Impact
- New permissions? No · Secrets changed? No · New network calls? No
